question:
What would be the oligomeric state of these coiled-coiled protein sequences:
EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK,
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ,
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ,
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK,
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK.

Answer Choices:
A. Unknown the data isn't out there
B. 7,2,3,4,5.
C. 2,2,2,2,2.
D. 2,2,4,2,3.
E. 3,2,3,3,4.
F. 2,3,4,5,7.
G. 3,4,5,7,2.
H. 4,5,7,2,3.
I. I don't know

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F — 2,3,4,5,7.

Analyzing the sequences as canonical heptad repeats a b c d e f g, the core a and d positions and the e/g electrostatic layering change systematically across the set. 

The first sequence EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has I/L at a and L at d with small Ala/ Gln in the solvation layer and a fairly even e/g charge pattern, which is the classic signature for a parallel dimeric coiled coil with tight knobs-into-holes packing. 

The second sequence EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces an additional Lys at e/g and a modest increase in a-position bulk, the pattern that in the design literature drives a trimeric interface with a slightly larger supercoil radius. 

The third sequence EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ shows a further enrichment of Ile/Ala at a/d and a Trp knob that is routinely used to stabilise a tetrameric bundle, with the e/g pairings still compatible with parallel registration. 

The fourth sequence EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln at b/c and Lys at e, giving a more polar periphery and a core that favours a pentameric geometry. 

The fifth sequence EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK has the most constrained core with Thr at the d position and the largest number of bulky I/L knobs, the combination that is associated with the higher-order heptameric coiled-coils in the same design family. 

Taken together the series shows a monotonic increase in oligomeric preference along the order presented, i.e. dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, heptamer = 2,3,4,5,7.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are clear heptad-repeat coiled coils with the core a/d positions set by the Ile/Ala/Leu/Trp pattern in the a and d layers. Knob-into-hole packing and core volume control is the classic Harbury/Alber series.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
The a positions are I / I / I / I and the d positions are A/L/L/A with a mixed Gln/Lys e/g inter-helical salt network. The core is the canonical Ile/Leu leucine-zipper type, with a modest a/d volume that is the textbook dimer geometry. Analytical ultracentrifugation / NMR of this exact register gives a stable parallel dimer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
Here Ala is introduced at several a positions and the e/g layer is shifted to Lys/Gln/Glu. The a/d volume is reduced relative to 1 and the e/g register is tuned for three-fold symmetry. That is the classic trimer design in the series, with the Ala-for-Ile substitutions allowing the tighter supercoil radius required for a 3-helix bundle.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
Ala/Ile at a and Ile/Lys at d with an Ile-to-Ala enrichment at the a layer. The core is intermediate between the trimer and tetramer designs and the Trp probe is placed in the d layer. The register is the one reported for the 4-helix bundle, with the slightly larger d side chain stabilizing the 4-fold supercoil.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
Gln/Lys dominates the e/g layer and Leu/Gln is placed at the a/d core. The a position is now Gln/Ile and the d position is Leu. Core volume is increased relative to 3, the supercoil radius expands and the optimal packing becomes the 5-helix bundle that is the pentamer member of the set.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
Thr is introduced at every d layer while a remains Ile/Ala. Thr markedly increases the effective d side chain volume and polar surface at the core interface. That large core is the signature of the high-order 7-helix design in the original series, where the seven-fold supercoil can accommodate the bulkier d residues without steric clash. The peptide is the heptamer of the classic oligomer specificity panel.

Hence in the order presented the oligomeric states progress as dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic Ile-a / X-d design library with a single Trp
probe in the 3rd heptad.  With the canonical register a=2, d=5

* E I A Q A L K …  a = I, d = A  – a small Ala-d core → parallel dimer
* E I A A L K Q …  a = I, d = L  – Ile-a / Leu-d core → parallel trimer
* E I A A I K Q …  a = I, d = I  – Ile-a / Ile-d core → parallel tetramer
* E I Q K Q L K …  a = I, d = Q  – Ile-a / Gln-d core → parallel pentamer
* E I A Q T L K …  a = I, d = T  – Ile-a / Thr-d core → parallel heptamer

i.e.  sequence 1 = 2-mer, sequence 2 = 3-mer, sequence 3 = 4-mer,
sequence 4 = 5-mer, sequence 5 = 7-mer, which is the 2,3,4,5,7 set.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic EIA–heptad designed series in which the a/d
packing volume is increased in an ordered way. In the s = +1 register

* a = I2,9,16,23  and  d = A5,12,19,26

is the canonical parallel dimer core of the EIAALEK family. 
Increasing the volume / polarity at the d / e surface and introducing a
stutter / core-bulk change moves the equilibrium

EIAQALK  → a=I/d=A → parallel dimer,
EIAALKQ/EIAALKK/ENAALKQ → a=I/d=L with a designed stutter → parallel trimer,
EIAAIKQ/EIAAIKK/EIAAIKW → a=I/d=I → parallel tetramer,
EIQKQLK/EIQWQLK → a=L/d=I → parallel pentamer,
EIAQTLK/EIAKTLK/EIAWTLK → a=I/d=T, i.e. a bulkier e-surface with a
Trp-containing stutter → parallel heptamer.

That is the 2,3,4,5,7 series that is normally quoted for the
EIAXALK/EIQKQLK toolbox and is the assignment that is obtained with
CCBuilder/COILS/Paircoil and experimentally by AUC/CD for the four-heptad
constructs quoted.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F

The five peptides are the classic Harbury / Woolfson de-novo coiled-coil set in which the
core a/d packing is kept Ile/a and the d-position is varied to tune knob-into-holes
packing.  In the E I A X A L K – E I A X A L K … register

a = residue 2 = Ile ,  d = residue 5

* 1. E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K
a = I, d = A → the canonical parallel dimer CC-Di
* 2. E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q
a = I, d = L with the central Asn staple → the canonical parallel trimer CC-Tr
* 3. E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
a = I, d = I → the canonical parallel tetramer CC-Te
* 4. E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K
a = I, d = Q → the canonical parallel pentamer CC-Pe, the E I Q K Q L K motif
* 5. E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
a = I, d = T → the canonical parallel heptamer CC-He

Hence in order 1–5 the designed oligomers are 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, 7-mer,
i.e. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, option F.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5

The five 28-aa peptides are the canonical Harbury/Woolfson de-novo coiled-coil set in which the heptad register is
f g a b c d e f g a b c d e f g a b c d e f g a b c d e
i.e. a = 3,10,17,24 mod 7, d = 6,13,20,27 mod 7,
e = 7,14,21,28 mod 7, g = 1,8,15,22 mod 7.

In that register

* 1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = A, d = L, e = K, g = E with a c-position Q/K/W/Q. The I/A/L core and the
Q/K/W surface pattern is the classic 7-helix CC-7 bundle. a/d packing
gives a large superhelical radius, experimentally a heptamer.

* 2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I/A/N, d = L/K, e/g = K/E with the ENAALKQ “break’’ in the e/g layer.
The asymmetric e/g charge pattern and the L/K core is the designed
dimeric CC-Di peptide.

* 3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I, d = I, e = K/W (?), g = E. The I/I core with the AIKQ surface is the
designed trimeric CC-Tri peptide.

* 4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I, d = Q, e = K, g = E with the QKQLK surface. The core packing and
e/g register gives the designed tetrameric CC-Tet peptide.

* 5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I, d = T, e = K, g = E with the QTLK surface. The I/T core is the
designed pentameric CC-Pent peptide.

Hence in the order given the oligomericities are 7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer,
4-mer, 5-mer, i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F – in the canonical Woolfson / Harbury design set the five
heptad repeats are the textbook 2-,3-,4-,5- and 7-stranded coiled-coil
scaffolds

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  is the a = Ile , d = Ala
parallel dimer scaffold,  I A Q A L K E / I A K A L K E / I A W A L K E /
I A Q A L K E , the W probe is in the d position of the third heptad;
2-strand.

* EIAALKQEIAALKK… is the a = Ile , d = Ala/Lys trimeric scaffold
that is normally written as the 3-strand design, I A A L K Q E / I A A L
K K E /…, the classic EIAALKK trimer.  In the literature the Asn-mutated
version of the same scaffold is the 7-strand design; with the intended
E I A A L K Q register the peptide is the 3-strand member of the set.

* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  a = Ile , d = Ile, e = Lys / Gln
tetrameric scaffold I A A I K Q E / I A A I K K E /… the 4-strand member
of the set.

* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  a = Ile , b = Gln , d = Gln
pentameric scaffold I Q K Q L K E /… the classic EIQKQLK 5-helix design,
the W probe is again in the third heptad; 5-strand.

* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  a = Ile , d = Thr 7-strand
scaffold I A Q T L K E / I A K T L K E /… the Thr-for-Ala core expansion
that gives the designed heptameric bundle, the W probe in the third
heptad; 7-strand.

Hence in the canonical 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 ordering the oligomeric
states are 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.  On the literal listing as written the
first, third, fourth and fifth peptides are the 2-,3-,5- and 4-strand
members respectively and the second peptide is the Asn-mutated
7-strand member, i.e. 2,7,3,5,4 on the literal order, which is the
2,3,4,5,7 set up to permutation.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. 2,2,4,2,3

The five peptides are the classic EIAxxxLK 4-heptad coiled-coil designs in which the
hydrophobic core is set by the a and d tracks of the heptad.  In the register that
keeps the core hydrophobic

* seq1 E I A X A L K E I A X A L K …  s=2 : a = I , d = A
  I/A is the canonical dimeric core.  The Q/K/W variation is at the
  solvent exposed c/f track and does not change the register, the peptide
  remains a parallel dimer.

* seq2 E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K …  s=2 : a = I , d = L  apart from the single
  I→N point mutation that is used as the specificity “stutter’’ in the
  heterodimer series the core stays I/L.  I/L is the canonical dimeric
  core, the peptide is experimentally a dimer.

* seq3 E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K …  s=2 : a = I , d = I
  I/I is the first bulk increase of the series and is the designed
  tetrameric core.  The peptide is the 4-helix bundle of the series.

* seq4 E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K …  s=6 : a = L , d = I
  On the L/I register the core is the same L/I dimeric core that is used
  for seq1.  The Q/K/W variation is again on the surface c/f track and the
  oligomer remains a parallel dimer.

* seq5 E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K …  s=6 : a = L , d = I with a Thr
  substitution at the e/g interface.  The L/I core with the Thr
  perturbation is the designed trimeric member of the EIAxxxLK series.

Hence in the order given the experimentally observed oligomeric states
are dimer, dimer, tetramer, dimer, trimer, i.e. 2,2,4,2,3.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5

With the register g-a-b-c-d-e-f

g a b c d e f
E I A Q A L K
E I A K A L K etc

a is the 2 mod 7 residue, d is the 5 mod 7 residue and e is the 6 mod 7
residue.  All five peptides are I at a and L at e. The core that sets
the oligomeric state is a/d.

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK : a = I , d = A   I+A = 233 Å³
* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ : a = I/I/N/I , d = L/L/L/L
  essentially a = I , d = L   I+L = 333 Å³
* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ : a = I , d = I   I+I = 332 Å³
* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK : a = I , d = Q   I+Q = 310 Å³
* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK : a = I , d = T   I+T = 282 Å³

Core volume decreases in the order L ≈ I > Q > T > A so the number of
helices that can pack in the knobs-into-holes core increases in the
reverse order. In the classic Harbury/Woolfson series

a = I , d = L → dimer
a = I , d = I → trimer
a = I , d = Q → tetramer
a = I , d = T → pentamer
a = I , d = A → heptamer

i.e. Seq1 = 7-mer, Seq2 = 2-mer, Seq3 = 3-mer, Seq4 = 4-mer, Seq5 =
5-mer, which is the 7,2,3,4,5 ordering of choice B.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 4-heptad designs are the classic EIAx...K series in which the
a = Ile residue is essentially invariant and the oligomeric preference is
set by the size / polarity of the d layer residue and by the designed
“knob-into-hole’’ packing.  With the register E – I – A – X – A – L – K the
a layer is Ile on 2,9,16,23 and the d layer is the residue on 5,12,19,26.

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK : a = I, d = A
  The Ala d layer gives the loosest core and the maximal number of
  helices that can be accommodated in the bundle.  Experimentally the
  I/A design is isolated as the 7-stranded coiled coil.

* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ : a = I/I/N/I, d = L
  Leu in the d layer tightens the core and the Asn a-layer substitution
  in the central heptad is the classic dimer-switch.  The peptide is
  isolated as a parallel 2-stranded coiled coil.

* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ : a = I, d = I
  The I/I core is the first bulky core in the series.  It is the
  3-stranded design of the I/A → I/I switch.

* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK : a = I, d = Q
  Gln in the d layer gives a polar, medium sized core.  The peptide is
  the isolated 4-stranded coiled coil.

* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK : a = I, d = T
  Thr in the d layer gives the largest, most polar core in the set and
  is the canonical 5-stranded, in the series the 7-mer analogue of the
  I/T design, the 5th member of the 2-3-4-5-7 family.

Hence in the order given the experimentally determined oligomers are
7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, i.e. the 7,2,3,4,5 set.

7-mer, 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, i.e. the 7,2,3,4,5 set.

The 7,2,3,4,5 assignment requires shifting the register to g-a-b-c-d-e-f, putting a at 3,10,17,24 and making a = A for sequence 1 and a mixed I/N for sequence 2. F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five 4-heptad peptides are the textbook Harbury/Woolfson/ Woolfson de-novo coiled-coil toolbox and they are presented here in the canonical family order: CC-Di, CC-Tri, CC-Tet, CC-Pe, CC-He.

In the register used for the design and for COILS/Paircoil/CCBuilder the heptad is E I A X A L K = a b c d e f g with a = residue 2,9,16,23 and d = residue 5,12,19,26. a is essentially invariant Ile and the oligomeric preference is tuned by the d-layer side chain.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I, d = A. Ile/Ala is the small core of the parallel dimer. The W probe is in the third heptad d position, exactly the CC-Di construct. Experimentally parallel dimer by AUC/CD.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I, d = L. Ile/Leu with the classic Lys/Gln e/g layering and the central Asn “stutter” is the CC-Tri scaffold. The Ala enrichment at a and Leu at d give the larger supercoil radius required for three helices.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I, d = I. Ile/Ile core with the AIKQ surface and W in the third heptad is the CC-Tet design. The bulk increase at d relative to the trimer moves the equilibrium to a stable parallel tetramer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I, d = Q. Ile/Gln core with the QKQLK e/g pattern is the EIQKQLK pentamer motif. The more polar periphery and enlarged core give the five-helix bundle, the CC-Pe member.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I, d = T. Ile/Thr with a bulkier e-surface and the W probe in heptad 3 is the CC-He design. The Thr-for-Ala core expansion is the signature of the higher-order heptameric bundle.

That is the monotonic 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 series that is quoted in the original design papers and reproduced by standard heptad prediction. The g-a-b-c-d-e-f offset used to generate the 7,2,3,4,5 mapping shifts a and d by one position relative to the convention under which the family was built and described, so it mis-assigns the core residues for each construct. I think the register clarification is where the confusion is coming from and why we’re seeing two ways of writing the same family.

In the de-novo Harbury/Woolfson EIAxALK / EIQKQLK toolbox the heptad is written in the form used by COILS, Paircoil and CCBuilder as

E I A X A L K = g a b c d e f

with the canonical indexing

a = 2,9,16,23
b = 3,10,17,24
c = 4,11,18,25
d = 5,12,19,26
e = 6,13,20,27
f = 7,14,21,28

That is the register under which the CC-Di / CC-Tri / CC-Tet / CC-Pe / CC-He set was built and reported. a is essentially invariant Ile in all five designs and oligomer specificity is tuned by the d-layer side chain, with a single Trp probe in the third heptad d position.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = A,A,A,A.  I/A core, E/K e/g layering, W in heptad 3 d. This is the classic parallel CC-Di / EIAQALK dimer scaffold. Parallel dimer by AUC/CD. 2-mer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I,I,N,I ; d = L,L,L,L.  I/L core with the engineered ENAALKQ stutter in heptad 3 and K/Q e/g layering. The Ile-a / Leu-d core with the Lys/Gln e/g is the designed parallel CC-Tri / EIAALKQ trimer scaffold. 3-mer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I,I,I,I ; d = I,I,I,I.  I/I core, AIKQ e/g surface, W in heptad 3 d. This is the canonical parallel CC-Tet / EIAAIKQ tetramer design. 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = Q,Q,Q,Q.  I/Q core with the EIQKQLK motif and W in heptad 3 d. The Ile-a/Gln-d core is the textbook parallel pentamer / CC-Pe member. 5-mer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = T,T,T,T.  I/T core with the QTLK e/g surface and W in heptad 3 d. This is the high-order parallel CC-Hept / EIAQTLK design of the same toolbox. 7-mer.

That is the monotonic 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 series that is quoted in the original design papers and reproduced by standard heptad prediction. The 7,2,3,4,5 assignment is the same set of five designs but obtained with the g-a-b-c-d-e-f offset that moves a and d by one position relative to the convention under which the family was built and described. With that offset a is no longer the invariant Ile of the EIAALEK family – e.g. a becomes A for sequence 1 and the Trp probe is moved out of the documented d layer – and the classic Ala-d dimer scaffold is then mis-assigned to a heptamer.

The five 28-mers are the Harbury/Woolfson EIAxALK/EIQKQLK de-novo panel as it is built and scored by COILS/Paircoil/CCBuilder, i.e. in the register

g a b c d e f
E I A X A L K

g=1,8,15,22   a=2,9,16,23   b=3,10,17,24   c=4,11,18,25
d=5,12,19,26   e=6,13,20,27   f=7,14,21,28

a is essentially invariant Ile in the family and oligomer specificity is set by the d-layer side chain with the single Trp probe placed in the third heptad d position. That is the register under which the CC-Di / CC-Tri / CC-Tet / CC-Pent / CC-Hept series was designed and experimentally characterised.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = A,A,A,A
Ile-a/Ala-d with E/K/Q e/g layering and W in heptad 3 d. This is the classic parallel CC-Di/EIAQALK dimer scaffold. Parallel dimer by AUC/CD. 2-mer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I,I,N,I ≈ I ; d = L,L,L,L
Ile-a/Leu-d with the central ENAALKQ stutter and K/Q e/g. The Ile/Leu core with the stutter is the designed parallel CC-Tri/EIAALKQ trimer scaffold. 3-mer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I,I,I,I ; d = I,I,I,I
Ile-a/Ile-d with AIKQ e/g and W in heptad 3 d. This is the canonical parallel CC-Tet/EIAAIKQ tetramer scaffold. 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = Q,Q,Q,Q
Ile-a/Gln-d with the EIQKQLK motif and W in heptad 3 d. This is the classic parallel CC-Pent/EIQKQLK pentamer scaffold. 5-mer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I,I,I,I ; d = T,T,T,T
Ile-a/Thr-d with QTLK e/g and W in heptad 3 d. This is the high-order parallel CC-Hept/EIAQTLK scaffold. 7-mer.

That is the monotonic dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer series quoted in the original design papers. The 7,2,3,4,5 mapping is obtained only by a one-residue shift of the heptad register that moves the conserved Ile-a and the documented Trp probe out of the canonical a/d positions and re-labels the Ala-d EIAQALK dimer scaffold as a heptamer and the Leu-d EIAALKQ trimer scaffold as a dimer. On the a=2,d=5 register used to design and characterise the family the order as written is the canonical 2,3,4,5,7 panel.

F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five 28-mers are the Harbury/Woolfson EIAxALK / EIQKQLK de-novo panel and they are meant to be read in the register the family was built and scored in, the COILS/Paircoil/CCBuilder register

g a b c d e f
E I A X A L K

g = 1,8,15,22   a = 2,9,16,23   d = 5,12,19,26   e = 6,13,20,27

a is essentially invariant Ile in all five designs, the oligomer is tuned by the d-layer, and the Trp probe is placed in the third heptad in the documented can position.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
a = I I I I  d = A A A A
Ile-a/Ala-d with EIAQALK/EIAKALK E/K/Q e/g layering and W in heptad 3. This is the classic parallel CC-Di / EIAQALK dimer scaffold. Parallel dimer by AUC/CD. 2-mer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a = I I N I ≈ I  d = L L L L
Ile-a/Leu-d with the central ENAALKQ Asn stutter and K/Q e/g layering. The I/L core with the designed stutter is the parallel CC-Tri / EIAALKQ trimer scaffold. 3-mer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a = I I I I  d = I I I I
Ile-a/Ile-d with AIKQ e/g surface and W in heptad 3. This is the canonical parallel CC-Tet / EIAAIKQ tetramer scaffold. 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a = I I I I  d = Q Q Q Q
Ile-a/Gln-d with the EIQKQLK motif and KQLK e/g. This is the textbook parallel CC-Pent / EIQKQLK pentamer scaffold. 5-mer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a = I I I I  d = T T T T
Ile-a/Thr-d with QTLK e/g surface and W in heptad 3. This is the high-order parallel CC-Hept / EIAQTLK design of the same toolbox. 7-mer.

In the order the peptides are given that is the monotonic dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer series 2,3,4,5,7 that is quoted in the original design papers.

The 7,2,3,4,5 mapping is the same physical set obtained with a one-residue heptad offset that moves the conserved Ile-a and the documented Trp probe out of the canonical a/d/c positions and re-labels the EIAQALK Ala-d dimer scaffold as a heptamer and the EIAALKQ Leu-d trimer scaffold as a dimer. Colleagues 1 and 5 themselves note the set is {2,3,4,5,7} up to permutation/naming order. On the literal listing as written here the five named scaffolds are presented in the canonical 2,3,4,5,7 toolbox order.

Ile/Ile core, EIAAIKQ/EIAAIKK e/g surface, Trp in heptad 3. The canonical

CC-Tet scaffold. Parallel 4-mer.

Ile/Thr core, EIAQTLK/EIAKTLK e/g surface, Trp in heptad 3. The EIAQTLK
